messages.author: 3fbf4f602341f5ec
messages.subject: Model comparison with procD.pgls?
parts:
Hello everyone,

I have four models that I am running using procD.pgls that I would like to compare somehow to see which is the best fit for my data. Is this possible? 

I have a matrix of 5 logged linear measurements as my response variables ('torso') that I include in the following models:

torso ~ logged body mass

torso ~ logged body mass + 6 continuous diet variables

torso ~ logged body mass + 6 continuous locomotor variables 

torso ~ logged body mass + diet vars + locomotor vars 

After some reading, I think I could calculate and compare AIC if I really wanted to but I was wondering if there was another way to compare these models (perhaps using advanced.procD.lm)?

Thank you very much,
Eve

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Model comparison with procD.pgls?
parts:
Eve,

The model.comparison function in the RRPP package might be appealing.  You can still perform AIC, but you have other options.  Additionally, the anova function via RRPP (anova.lm.rrpp) functions like a likelihood ratio test for multiple models.  Examples are provided in the help pages, and there is a vignette.  I recommend installing from github to get the most up-to-date version, i.e.,

devtools::install_github(“mlcollyer/RRPP”)

Both RRPP and geomorph use the same RRPP framework, but RRPP is more bare bones whereas geomorph is more morphometric-focused.

If you wish to stay within geomorph, the advanced.procD.lm function can compare two models.  You could do a few pairwise model comparisons, test by test.  The anova.lm.rrpp function uses the same concept, but allows for more models, and has additional output (like confidence intervals for test statistics).

Hope that helps!
Mike

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Model comparison with procD.pgls?
parts:
Eve,

You will have to create objects of class lm.rrpp, which will have basically the same parts as procD.lm (plus other things).  There are two steps that will make this possible.

1) Convert coordinates from a gpagen object to a data matrix using the two.d.array function.  RRPP will nto know what to do with coordinates in a 3D array.
2) Generate a phylogenetic covariance matrix for input to lm.rrpp.  For some geomorph functions, we do this internally.  With RRPP it must be done explicitly.

Once these things are done, the exact same coefficients and other stats are generated via lm.rrpp as you would expect with procD.lm.  

Hope that helps!
Mike

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Model comparison with procD.pgls?
parts:
Eve,

 

Geomorph’s PGLS functions do not have the ability to use lambda, Kappa, or other parameters to ‘stretch’ the internal branches of the phylogeny. I am personally wary of such approaches, as I don’t think they are doing what people think they are.  Regardless, when they are used, they are based on the response variables only: not the regression relationship itself (in other words, the value of lambda is based on the Y-data only).

 

That said, I believe your original goal was to understand how phylogeny ‘influences’ your PGLS results. It is not clear to me what that means. PGLS is simply a weighted least squares regression, where the regression relationship is weighted inversely by species non-independence. The point of this is to properly model the fact that one’s data points (species) are not independent; they are related phylogenetically. Procedurally this means that instead of having independent error in the regression (Y = Xb + e), the error is structured by the phylogeny to reflect the non-independence. Thus the ‘influence’ is a purposeful one: we know the species are not independent and so we must incorporate the phylogeny to account for this.

 

So I’m not sure what additional component needs to be evaluated here: unless I have misunderstood the question.

 

Dean
